note: Both sets share the same 22 dishwasher and clothes-drying claims, including the same redundancies (the 120°F/48.9°C threshold stated three times, 115°F twice, heated-drying and cycle-completion rules twice) and the same trivial Figure 8 axis-tick claim. B adds two claims: the important laundry eligibility rule (complete, uninterrupted washer cycle), which A omits entirely, and a Figure 8 'scoring function' claim listing 90, 100, 110, 120 as points, which misreads the x-axis (% of original weight) tick values as point values. A is error-free but drops an important rule; B is net more complete and faithful despite one misread figure claim.
remarks: Both sets miss several substantive facts on the page: the two-loads-per-day / separately-scored rule (item d), permitted drying methods and the visibility/demonstration requirement (item c), the temperature-of-record rule (higher of two sensors unless the higher one is defective), the definition of cycle 'interruption' (item e), the 'normal'/'regular' setting selection rule (item g), and the allowed load states (empty, partial, full; soiled or clean, item h). Both sets also heavily duplicate the same facts under different attribute names (e.g., 'required temperature sensor peak', 'temperature sensor minimum value for full points', and the °C restatement all encode the 120°F threshold), which inflates claim counts without adding information. The Figure 8 y-axis (points per clothes drying task) has no numeric labels in the text layer, so any point values attributed to it are unsupported.
